Here already

This tune’s named as Harvest Moon and is here already though the setting is obviously a bit different.
https://thesession.org/tunes/3679
The usual questions arise as to whether this should just be posted as a comment in the other entry or are they different enough to warrant separate entries.
I do suspect that Harvest Moon is the correct name for the tune and when tunes get someone’s name appended it sometimes means nothing more than that that was the source.
On checking the Fiddler’s Companion it appears that this is a tune written by the late Paddy O’Brien (Tipperary).
--“HARVEST MOON, THE [2]. AKA - ”Paddy O‘Brien’s.“ Irish, Reel. A Dorian. Standard. Composed by the late button accordion player Paddy O’Brien. PTI 1041, James and John Kelly - ”Irish Traditional Fiddle Music“ (appears as second reel of ”London Set“). Martin Connolly - ”Back in Brooklyn."

Harvest Moon, X:9

Inspired by a recording of Paddy Carty, and after a few years of Niall Keegan bashing my head in I’ve arrived at this. This is a fun flute version that I think does justice to what John Wynne would call, “the virtuoso” style of Roscommon flute playing. While that debate about regional styles should be left to those far more erudite, (or perhaps, far more full of $%#@) we know Paddy was not afraid to use keys that many of his contemporaries would not have used in those days. Thus the A minor key that hints at a harmonic minor scale, before returning to A dorian in the second part. I like to think of this as a fanciful “what if” setting not safe for the session.

If only I did more of this in college instead of going to Costello’s to drink and see Flan. (Who claims to have played with *the* Sean Ryan back in the day!)

Hate mail inbound in 3…2…1…

Harvest Moon, X:10

This is the version from Adam Agee & Jon Sousa on Ceol na gCarad. There it’s called The Old Favorite, but it’s definitely this tune! Not notated is the lovely crunchy triple that happens each time at the cdeg run in both the A and B parts.
